result_text:
The scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java` now match the new rules. The four existing test classes for the scoping code pass (`CodeConfigurationTest`, `SourceCodeFilesTest`, `SourceFileFilterTest`, `SourceFileTest`, 23 tests in total). Nothing is committed.

Changes, all in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **Hidden-files ignore removed.** The `.*/[.][a-zA-Z0-9_]+.*` "Hidden files and folders" rule is replaced by `(.*/)?[.](git|svn|hg|bzr)/.*`, which ignores only version-control metadata. The `(.*/)?` prefix lets it match a path that starts directly with `.git/`, as well as nested ones. `.gitignore` is not matched because the rule requires a slash after the folder name.
- **IDE and build-tool folders reclassified.** `(.*/)?[.](idea|vscode|vs|gradle|mvn|settings|metadata|circleci)/.*` is added to the build-and-deployment conventions, just before the `buildscripts` rule.
- **`dependencies` no longer ignored.** The `.*/dependencies/.*` ignore rule is deleted.

The `.yarn/releases`, `.yarn/plugins`, `node_modules` and `vendor` rules are untouched.

I did not check the new regexes against sample paths at runtime: a scratch program was denied permission to run. I checked them by reading only, so a quick runtime check is still worth doing.
